_about: WO57 §3: eBay's selling fees for a seller WITHOUT a store (ebay.com, US), as thrift_agent/ebay/fees.py reads them: the final value fee is a share of the TOTAL amount of the sale (item price + what the buyer pays for shipping + sales tax), by category, plus a per-order fee. `checked` is the day these numbers were compared with eBay's fee page; `thrift doctor` shows it and ONE private line says so when it is 90 days old. A rule applies to a listing whose category — or any of its ancestors — is one of `categories` (eBay category ids, EBAY_US tree); the first rule that applies wins, else `default`. `tiers`: the rate on the part of the total up to `up_to`, then the next. `when_total_at_least`: the rule applies only to a sale whose total reaches it (below it the next matching rule, else `default`). `order_fee: false`: no per-order fee under this rule. NOT in this file (2026-11-10): eBay's lower rates on a very large sale (the part above $7,500 in most categories, above $2,000 for bags) — a price worked out without them is a little higher than needed, never lower; add a tier (`up_to`) when a sale that large is in sight.
